title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): X is a conformal sphere and G = Aut_conf(X) is the group of Möbius and anti-Möbius maps. Grothendieck is classifying normalized round (spherical) Riemannian metrics compatible with the conformal structure, and in particular those invariant under a compact subgroup H. The next page states the resulting Proposition: existence; uniqueness iff X^H is empty; and the cases card X^H = 2 or H = {1, σ} with σ an inversion.

This page has two parts.

(1) End of an argument. Normalize X = P^1(C) with {z, z'} = {0, ∞}. T = {z ↦ az : |a| = 1} is the compact torus fixing the poles. σ(z) = b/z̄ with b > 0 is the inversion in the circle C = {z z̄ = b}, and σ' = ε∘σ, z ↦ -b/z̄, is the other T-commuting anti-holomorphic involution. Grothendieck checks two things about σ':
- it exchanges 0 and ∞;
- it preserves C, since (σ'z)·conj(σ'z) = (-b/z̄)(-b/z) = b²/(z z̄) = b when z z̄ = b.
Hence σ' together with (T, {0, ∞}) determines the same great circle C, i.e. the same spherical metric: σ' is the antipodal map of the round metric whose equator is C. This yields the 'contradiction' that closes an argument by contradiction begun on the previous page; the hypothesis being refuted is not visible on this page. The upshot is that the inversion/antipode ambiguity of order 2 does not affect the metric.

(2) The group N of conformal or anticonformal maps preserving T and fixing the two poles. N is an extension of Z/2 by T.
- For σ ∈ N \ T one has σz = a z̄, and σ²z = a ā z.
- σ² ∈ T forces |a| = 1, which in fact gives σ² = 1. So the extension splits: N ≅ U ⋊ Z/2 ≅ O(2).
- u_θ σ (θ ∈ U) has the same form, z ↦ (θa) z̄.
- Writing a = α² = α/ᾱ with α ∈ U, the fixed set is z = a z̄ ⇔ z/α ∈ R ⇔ z ∈ αR, a line through 0.
So the elements of N \ T are exactly the reflections in great circles through the poles.

The margin remarks that N = T ∪ N⁻, where N⁻ is the set of anti-involutions fixing {z, z'}; N is thus determined by {z, z'} alone. It then raises the question of extracting a spherical metric from such data.

Modern picture: compatible normalized round metrics on a conformal sphere are the points of hyperbolic 3-space H³ = PSL2(C)/PSU(2), equivalently the maximal compact subgroups PO(3). H-invariant metrics form the fixed set of H in H³, which is a totally geodesic subspace:
- a single point (unique metric);
- a geodesic (H stabilizes the pair {z, z'}; the metrics form a 1-parameter family indexed by T-orbits);
- a plane (H = {1, σ} with σ an inversion; the metrics are parametrized by (X \ X^σ)/σ, a disk model of H²);
- all of H³ (H trivial).
This page supplies the elementary computations in the torus case.
errors: No mathematical error. The computations (σ'² = id, σ'(C) = C, σ² = |a|² z, splitting, fixed line αR) are all correct.

N must be read as the stabilizer of each pole (normalizing T), not the full normalizer of T. The maps z ↦ b/z̄ also normalize T (indeed commute with it) but swap the poles, so they are excluded from N \ T here.
The 'contradiction' closes an argument whose hypothesis is not visible on this page, so the logic cannot be fully checked from this page alone.

ideas.what: Antipodal map and circle inversion attached to the same equator determine the same round metric (order-2 ambiguity is harmless).
ideas.modern_name: Antipodal map / reflection of the round sphere; maximal compact PO(3) containing the torus

ideas.what: Anti-conformal maps fixing two points and normalizing the rotation torus form a split extension O(2) = U ⋊ Z/2; its reflections fix lines αR.
ideas.modern_name: Normalizer of a maximal torus in PO(3) / O(2)

ideas.what: Classification of round metrics invariant under a compact group of conformal automorphisms of the sphere via fixed data (two points, or a circle).
ideas.modern_name: Fixed-point sets of compact subgroups of Isom(H³) acting on H³ = space of round metrics (Cartan fixed point theorem)

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary, correct computations in Möbius geometry, part of a lemma on invariant spherical metrics. The general statement is standard once round metrics are identified with points of H³. Grothendieck works without that identification, which is of mild biographical interest for the 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' project, but nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 reads roughly 'l'anti-holomorphe [involutif?] σ'z = -b/z̄ {+intervertit+} 0 et ∞'. The superscripted insertion is 'intervertit' (replacing struck 'transforme'), not 'i.e. involutif'.
'N est est une extension de γ par T': the symbol is unclear, probably Z/2 or {±1} (the quotient N/T of order 2).

Margin, best reading: 'Ici N est déterminé en termes de T, i.e. en termes de {z,z'}, comme T ∪ N⁻, où N⁻ est formé de toutes les anti-involutions de X qui fixent {z,z'}. Donc il suit une question ... d'extraire une métrique riemannienne sphérique'.
Line 'z ∈ C^σ ⟺ z = α z̄/ᾱ': the image shows z = α·(z̄/ᾱ) written with a stacked bar fraction, consistent with a = α/ᾱ.
